figures.finding: A minor may make a contract (other than a delegation of power or one over real property) as an adult does, but may disaffirm it before eighteen or within a reasonable time after, without returning what was received; Guam's law has no court-approval route that bars disaffirmance and no set-aside of earnings.

value.rule: may contract as an adult, subject to disaffirmance (19 GCA § 1107-1108)

figures.applies: The rule reaches every contract, so writing, directing and producing deals as well as performing. Guam's Code, unlike California's Family Code 6750-6753 which it otherwise resembles, carries no court approval or trust for a minor's entertainment contract in this chapter (my reading of the chapter's list of sections, 1101-1112).

sources.said: A minor may make any other contract than as above specified, in the same manner as an adult, subject … only to his power of disaffirmance under the provisions of this Chapter
the contract of a minor if made while … he is under the age of 18 may be disaffirmed by the minor himself, either before his majority or within a … reasonable time afterwards

figures.finding: A minor under sixteen needs an employment certificate the Wage and Hour Commissioner issues, kept by the employer; the Commissioner may set by regulation the conditions for those under sixteen working as entertainers, motion picture or theatrical performers; 14 and 15 year olds may not work in school hours, before 7am or after 7pm (9pm in summer), more than 3 hours on a school day, 18 in a school week, 8 on a non-school day or 40 in a non-school week; anyone under 18 gets a 30-minute break after 4 hours.

value.permit: Minor's Employment Certificate, Wage and Hour Commissioner (19 GCA § 11104)
value.performerRules: by the Commissioner's regulations (§ 11108(c)), not read
value.schoolHours: no work during required school attendance under 18

figures.applies: The certificate covers any work by a minor under sixteen, so a young writer or director employed on a production needs it as a performer does; the performer-specific regulations weren't read (blocker).

sources.said: No minor under the age of sixteen (16) years of age shall be employed … or permitted to work until the employer of such minor procures and keeps … on file an employment certificate for such minor issued by the … Commissioner pursuant to regulations.

Working conditions and circumstances under which minors … below the age of sixteen (16) years may be employed or permitted to … work as dancers, singers, musicians, entertainers, motion picture or … theatrical performers.

No minor aged fourteen (14) or fifteen (15) shall be employed … during school hours except as provided in school work experience or career … exploration programs; and not before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m., or after 9 p.m. … from June 1st through Labor Day; no minor aged fourteen (14) or fifteen … (15) shall work more than three (3) hours a day on school days nor more … than eighteen (18) hours a week in school weeks, nor more than eight (8) … hours a day on non-school days, and not more than forty (40) hours a week … in non-school weeks.
